text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall — high CPU and repeated OOMKilled on tokenizer pods in us-west-2 (svc: inference-tokenizer). First alerts at ~1792104444. Autoscaler reports spike in request concurrency.

Alex Chen: I'm awake, looking. seeing multiple pods restart loops, kube events show OOMKilled and then pod evictions.

Maria Gomez: Confirmed. Stack traces in logs show tokenizer memory blowup during heavy prompt parsing (long prompt bundles). Also a few containers printed `cuda: unhandled CUDA error` right before the crash on gpu-backed nodes.

Samir Patel: Copy. Can you paste a snippet of the kubelet events / container log?

Alex Chen: Pasting relevant bits:
```
kubelet: Pod inference-tokenizer-7d9c OOMKilled - rss: 8200Mi, limit: 8192Mi
containerd: signal 9 (SIGKILL)
runtime: runtime/cgo: CUDA driver lost: driver shutting down
```

Maria Gomez: Also seeing a flood of tiny prompt parsing requests from a single customer workspace (workspace_id: ws_44). They sent a batch of 10k short messages to our prompt-parsing endpoint causing many concurrent tokenizer invocations.

Jitendra Rao: That customer traffic pattern explains the concurrency spike. We need short-term mitigations: 1) throttle that workspace, 2) scale tokenizer pool horizontally, 3) reduce per-pod concurrency / set GOMAXPROCS for tokenizer to avoid memory blowouts.

InfraBot: Autoscaler action: added 3 nodes (g5.xlarge), but pods still OOM on new nodes due to per-process memory spike.

Samir Patel: Proposed immediate changes: set a per-request token limit and add a tokenizer queueing gate. I can push a temporary gate at the ingress (edge) layer to reject or rate-limit the offending workspace.

Alex Chen: On it. Rate-limiting rule pushed to edge: `workspace:ws_44` -> limit 100 rps (previously unlimited). Applying now.

Oncall Bot: @Alex Chen acknowledged. Please update when stable.

Maria Gomez: While edge throttle is going in, we should change pod resource request/limits and reduce concurrency. I'll prepare a k8s patch to set `CONCURRENCY=2` for tokenizer deployment and bump memory limit to 12Gi temporarily.

Jitendra Rao: Caution — bumping limits delays OOM but doesn't fix leak. Also make sure HPA doesn't auto-scale unbounded; set maxReplicas=50 for this incident.

Alex Chen: Pushed k8s patch: environment CONCURRENCY=2, memory limit -> 12Gi, maxReplicas=50. Rolling restart started.

Maria Gomez: Rolling restart is moving pods to new config. Watching logs.

InfraBot: New pods scheduled on g5 nodes. 3 pods went healthy, 2 still OOMKilled (old images).

Samir Patel: For the CUDA errors — those look like downstream effects of abrupt OOM. Not primary cause. Main issue is tokenizer allocating large contiguous buffers for some malformed prompt sequences.

Alex Chen: We added a temporary guard in tokenizer config: if tokenized_length > 20000 -> abort early and return 413 to caller. That should stop the pathological cases.

Linda Park: I've notified CS about possible customer impact on ws_44 and a handful of customers hitting large prompts. CS escalated a support ticket.

Maria Gomez: After throttle + concurrency reduction + token cap we see CPU utilization drop from 95% -> 40% on tokenizer pods. No new OOMs in the last 4 minutes.

Jitendra Rao: Good. Marking incident as "mitigated" for production traffic. Actions remaining: full root-cause triage, fix tokenizer streaming allocation, unit test for huge prompts, and add workspace-level rate limits in prod gating.

Samir Patel: I'll open a PR with allocator fix and add a streaming tokenization path that bounds memory. Will attach perf tests.

Alex Chen: Handing off to next oncall for monitoring and follow-up. Oncall shift change in 20m. @Jitendra — can you take on the 2hr watch?

Jitendra Rao: Taking the handoff. I'll watch for any re-occurrence and confirm customer outreach.

Oncall Bot: Handoff acknowledged. Next oncall: Jitendra Rao (2h watch).

Incident Bot: Incident state: MITIGATED — rate-limits + concurrency caps + token cap applied. Impact: degraded or failed requests for clients submitting extremely large prompt bundles; ~12 pods OOMKilled, primary region: us-west-2.

Linda Park: CS note: affected customers (ws_44 and 3 more) have been notified; support ticket numbers #9981, #9982. No paid customer SLA misses confirmed yet; tracking latency spikes for 5 customers.

Maria Gomez: Postmortem TODOs:
- root cause: tokenizer unbounded allocation for malformed prompt sequences
- short-term mitigations (done): workspace throttle, token cap, reduce per-pod concurrency, bump memory limits
- long-term fixes: streaming tokenizer, unit tests, telemetry for per-request tokenized size, circuit-breaker on model-serving path, improved autoscaler signals (mem-based)

Samir Patel: I'll attach logs and a diff of the temporary ingress rule to the incident doc.

Alex Chen: Final check: no new OOMs in last 20m, 0 pod restarts in the new deployment. I’m going offline for the day, Jitendra — ping me if it flares. :thumbsup:

Jitendra Rao: Will do. Creating incident doc now and scheduling a follow-up postmortem meeting for tomorrow 10am PT.

Oncall Bot: Incident thread closed to new pages. Please use incident-doc link when available. :lock:
